section_summary: This section contains forms, ordinances, cabinet orders and explanatory procedures for Japan’s new foreign exchange and export controls in December 1949. It covers export licensing and bank certification, collection of export proceeds, permitted currencies and exchange rates, licensing of foreign exchange businesses, appeals, and preparation of the foreign exchange budget. The final page is a State Department transfer sheet.

subfiles.title: Application for License to Export (Form IE 234)
subfiles.to: Ministry of International Trade and Industry
subfiles.about: Form for approval of exports requiring a license.
subfiles.summary: Records buyer, goods, destination, payment terms, ministry approval, SCAP validation and commercial bank certification.

subfiles.title: Report on Collection of Export Proceeds
subfiles.to: Minister of International Trade and Industry
subfiles.about: Form for reporting collection of export proceeds.
subfiles.summary: Requests license and bank numbers, amounts collected, collection method, balance and arrangements for collection.

subfiles.title: Ordinance Fixing the Form of Export Declaration
subfiles.from: Prime Minister’s Office; Ministry of Finance; Ministry of International Trade and Industry
subfiles.about: Prescribes the new export declaration form.
subfiles.summary: Establishes the declaration’s format under customs and export control law. The annexed form records shipment particulars, bank clearance, payment arrangements, customs examination and foreign exchange settlement.

subfiles.title: Export Procedures after 1 December 1949
subfiles.from: Office of the U.S. Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Explains the procedures governing private exports after the December 1949 reforms.
subfiles.summary: Ordinary exports generally proceed through a bank-certified export declaration, while specified commodities, contracts and payment methods still require MITI licensing. The memorandum details bank checks, customs clearance, shipment suspension, export pricing, collection of proceeds, yen payment, raw-material allocation and post-shipment review. It also explains exemptions for low-value goods and free samples, and inspection requirements for controlled products.

subfiles.title: Ministry of Finance Ordinance No. 101
subfiles.doc_type: ministerial ordinance and annexed application form
subfiles.about: Designates currencies for foreign payments and provides a form for exceptions.
subfiles.summary: Designates United States and United Kingdom currencies for settlement under the Foreign Exchange and Foreign Trade Control Law. Other currencies require Finance Ministry authorization using the annexed application.

subfiles.title: Ministry of Finance Ordinance No. 102
subfiles.doc_type: ministerial ordinance and annexed application forms
subfiles.about: Sets licensing procedures for foreign exchange and money changing businesses.
subfiles.summary: Defines foreign exchange and money changing business and requires applications for licenses and for new or changed offices. Annexed forms ask banks about proposed operations, staffing, expected transactions and reasons for the application.

subfiles.title: Ministry of Finance Notification No. 970
subfiles.about: Establishes basic and cross rates of foreign exchange.
subfiles.summary: Sets rates of ¥360 per U.S. dollar and ¥1,008 per pound sterling.

subfiles.title: Cabinet Order No. 378: Reports by Foreign Exchange Banks and Money Changers
subfiles.to: Foreign exchange banks and money changers
subfiles.about: Requires business reports and addresses existing authorizations during the transition to the new law.
subfiles.summary: Requires periodic reports and permits the Ministers of Finance and International Trade and Industry to collect business information. Supplementary provisions carry forward certain earlier licenses and banking arrangements.

subfiles.title: Cabinet Order on Petition, Notice, Hearing and Decision
subfiles.about: Sets procedures for appeals under the Foreign Exchange and Foreign Trade Control Law.
subfiles.summary: Prescribes written petitions, grounds for dismissal, notice of public hearings and hearing procedure. It also specifies minutes, access to the record, reasoned decisions and requests for copies.

subfiles.title: Cabinet Order Concerning Ministerial Council
subfiles.about: Establishes the Ministerial Council responsible for the foreign exchange budget.
subfiles.summary: Names the council’s membership and advisory role and assigns secretarial work to the Economic Stabilization Board. It specifies quarterly estimates and the classification of proposed foreign exchange budgets by imports, uses, currencies and relevant agreements.

subfiles.title: Fiscal Regulation Concerning Export Trade
subfiles.about: Sets standard export payment methods and bank reporting requirements.
subfiles.summary: Defines designated currencies, standard letters of credit and prepayment arrangements, and banks’ duties to report credits, changes and risks to collection. Attachment 1 lists territories whose exports are paid in sterling; Attachment 2 lists special payment arrangements by country or area; Attachment 3 supplies a credit reporting form.

subfiles.title: Foreign Exchange Control Board Notification No. 1
subfiles.from: Nobutane Kiuchi, Chairman, Foreign Exchange Control Board
subfiles.to: Foreign exchange banks and money changers
subfiles.about: Sets buying and selling rates for U.S. and U.K. currencies.
subfiles.summary: Specifies Board and commercial rates, effective December 5, with temporary Board rates through December 4.

subfiles.title: Department of State Transfer Sheet (Form DS-202)
subfiles.from: Department of State, Division of Communications and Records
subfiles.about: Records transfer of a correspondence item to another file number.
subfiles.summary: The handwritten source, destination and transfer date are not reliably legible in the OCR.
